quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: ____ your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only blood alcohol levels above the legal limit can reduce
Alcohol does not reduce
Even a small amount of alcohol can reduce
Only blood alcohol levels above 0.05 percent can reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can reduce
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: A good rule for passing other vehicles is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever you can.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Move to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and use your horn to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass another vehicle, the risk of a crash increases. If you drive faster than other traffic, you will need to pass continuously. Drive with traffic flow at the legal speed limit and pass only when needed.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep downhill grade ahead.
Winding road.
Merging traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downhill grade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: When driving on icy or snowy roads, what technique helps prevent crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve grip.
Leave the highways as soon as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and increase the distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase the distance between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snowy or icy roads. This and increasing your following distance are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in each direction, even if you must enter the intersection.
Stop where you have a clear view of oncoming traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you have a clear view of oncoming traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the nearest point to the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less serious with beer than wine.
Is less serious with wine than beer.
Is worst with hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol harm your reflexes and judgment. What matters is not the type of drink, but how much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload items.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you may only stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done what you can.
Wait for police to arrive.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: Stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: When visibility decreases, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slowing down should be your first response when visibility becomes poor and road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: Highway signs that show information about dangerous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about possible dangers ahead. Always follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign can cause an accident.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest thing to do is:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other cars.
Drive slower than other cars.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Always drive at the same speed as the traffic around you. Stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: You are on a narrow road and meet a car coming toward you. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other car at least half of the road.
Tell the other car to pull over for you.
Turn on your high beams so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other car at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give cars going the opposite direction at least half the road. Both drivers need enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:

options.text: Alcohol.
Amphetamines.
Anger.
Driving with teenagers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol.
questions.explanation: Tiredness and alcohol have the same effects on driving. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving as much as a 0.05% blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours straight affects driving like a 0.10% blood alcohol level.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are crossing.
Continue driving because you have the right of way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mark dangerous intersections. Treat them exactly like stop signs.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when it is safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass other cars.

questions.question: A license plate frame:

options.text: Can cover the word "Missouri" on the plate.
Should not cover any part of the plate.
Can cover the month and year stickers.
Can cover the words at the bottom of the plate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not cover any part of the plate.
questions.explanation: Missouri law says license plates must be fastened securely and all parts must be visible and clean. Frames cannot cover any part of the plate.

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do it safely and without interfering with other cars.

questions.question: If your wheels go off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking. Turn carefully back onto the pavement. Check for nearby traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, slow down and move away from it if you can. If there is only one lane, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much space as possible. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or back so they can see you.

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no vehicle can cross the center line to pass, from either direction.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing on a two-lane road, move back to the right side when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
